exp.desc:
- Reception and appointments
- Repeat prescriptions
- ECG preparation

cl.p1: I have just completed a health and social care course with a placement at an internal medicine practice. I would now like to join a GP surgery because I value getting to know patients over many years.
cl.p2: On placement I worked on reception, booked appointments, handled repeat prescription requests and helped prepare patients for ECGs. I learned to juggle a full phone line, an impatient patient and a referral letter without anyone being forgotten. It never got boring.
cl.p3: I have known your practice as a patient since I was a child. I can start in August and would be glad to come in for a trial day.

cl.p1: After three years of parental leave with two children, I would like to return to my profession. Your advert for a morning role fits exactly: Monday to Friday, 7.30 to 12.00.
cl.p2: Before my leave I spent six years at a paediatric clinic. Preparing check-ups, hearing and sight tests and judging on the phone whether a child should be seen today were part of every day. I took a refresher course on practice emergencies last autumn.
cl.p3: I know systems have changed and I learn quickly. Childcare is in place from January.
